claims.statement: Ma, Xu, Dong, Sun, arXiv:1802.09806v4 (Phys. Rev. E 98, 042112 (2018)), 'Universal constraint for efficiency and power of a low-dissipation heat engine': low-dissipation model Q_x = Q_x^(r) - M_x/t_x (Eq. 2), P and eta (Eqs. 3-4), Eq. (1) universal bound, eta~+ over th+tc = tau+ (Eqs. 10-11), Eq. (13) closed form, asymmetry zeta (Eq. 14), 'it is not a supremum for all the P~' (p. 3), Appendix B: 'the analytical proof of its monotonicity is tedious and difficult. Instead numerical calculate the derivative'.

Ma & Fu, arXiv:2411.03849 (Phys. Rev. E 112, 054130 (2025)), 'Unified approach to power-efficiency trade-off relations of generic thermal machines', Appendix B: analytic proof (sign of d eta~+/d delta) that their upper bound increases in the dissipation ratio delta in [0,1]; at delta = 1 it is Eq. (1) of Ma et al. 2018. Their family is a different interpolation: it agrees with the root form at zeta = -1 (delta=0) and zeta = 1 (delta=1) but differs in between (max 0.038 under delta=(1+zeta)/2; 0.40 and 0.055 under two other natural maps; auditor script mafu_cmp.py).

Zhai, arXiv:2605.02732 (2026), 'Geometric Formulation of Power-Efficiency Bounds in Carnot-like Engines': re-derives Eq. (1) by a short geometric / linear-programming argument (as reported in AUDIT.md section 5). Zhai, Yue, Sun, arXiv:2509.07721, 'Exact bound of power-efficiency trade-off in finite-time thermodynamic cycles': state that Ma et al. 2018 already rigorously proved the Holubec-Ryabov conjecture and give an exact, tighter bound.

Holubec & Ryabov, arXiv:1603.02551 (J. Stat. Mech. (2016) 073204), 'Maximum Efficiency of Low-Dissipation Heat Engines at Arbitrary Power': their Eq. (34) upper bound equals Eq. (1); derived analytically only near P~ = 0 and P~ = 1, numerical evidence in between (read by the auditor). Ye & Holubec 2021 (arXiv:2112.08923) concerns heat pumps, not relevant. Esposito et al. 2010 (efficiency at maximum power bounds eta_C/2 <= eta* <= eta_C/(2-eta_C)) was NOT re-read; only used as the positive control at P~=1.

Hand derivation of the root form from the paper's model (code/derivation.md steps 1-4, with step 3 as corrected by audit correction 6): eta = u c, w = sqrt(1-eta); q(1-u) = w^2 a^2/th + b^2/tc; Cauchy-Schwarz gives q(1-u) tau+ >= (wa+b)^2 on th+tc <= tau+, with q tau+ = K M, K = 2/(1-sqrt(1-P~)); eta~+ is the largest u for which this holds, i.e. the MAXIMUM of eta over th+tc = tau+, an upper bound at power P that is not attained in general (the efficiency Cauchy-Schwarz equality needs th/tc = w a/b, the power equality th/tc = a/b); G(w,zeta) = K(w^2-(1-c)) - c((1-zeta)+(1+zeta)w)^2/4 is a convex quadratic with G(0)<0, so the feasible set is w >= w+ and eta~+/eta_C = (1-w+^2)/c. Checked independently by the auditor (AUDIT.md section 1). Not in Lean.

Eq. (13) as printed equals the root form. Symbolic (sympy, auditor): eliminating w from the tangency equality by squaring twice gives a quadratic R(u)=0; R(u13(x)) reduces to 0 modulo x^2 - radicand, so both sign branches of Eq. (13) are exact roots of R once square roots are squared away (an identity). Branch selection numerical (mpmath, 50 digits, 5000 random (c,P~,zeta)): the + branch matches the root form to 5.0e-48, the - branch is off by up to 0.47, the 'term inside the root' misreading by up to 0.23; minimum radicand 2.0e-3 > 0. Producer: 3000 random points at 60 digits, max |difference| 1.6e-58. None of this is in Lean; the branch choice is numerical only. The producer's preregistered transcription of Eq. (13) was wrong (the term -((1+zeta)/4) eta_C (1-sqrt(1-P)) put inside the root); the original disagreement (up to 0.23) is kept in logs/link_first_transcription.log.txt.

Controls, run before the headline: P1 Esposito sandwich (Lean + numerics: exact 1/2 and 1/(2-c) at P~=1); P2 exact rational instance (roots 5/7, 1/5); P3 Eq. (13) transcription agreement after the correction; N1 perturbed factor (zeta -> -zeta): perturbed roots increase, perturbed eta decreases 49/50 -> 1/2, grid 15,200/15,200 pairs non-increasing (the Lean pert_eta_not_mono only restates instance values, a weak control); N2 B sign flipped (5,920 bad pairs), K halved (611), C sign flipped (13,256, 558 undefined): all caught, true formula 0; N3 planted sorry and axiom caught by the axiom gate (LD-A-0003); N4 mistyped Eq. (13) (sign of zeta inside the root) differs by up to 0.156; perturbed Eq. (1) (1-c -> 1+c) violated by 11,522 of 17,355 random engines (auditor: 20,112 of 53,021).

HEADLINE (model-conditional, elementary). In the phenomenological low-dissipation Carnot model (Eqs. (2)-(4)), with the paper's eta~+ defined by the root form of the tangency quadratic: (i) eta~+ is strictly increasing in the asymmetry zeta on the whole box 0<c<1, K>1, zeta in [-1,1] (Lean, Tier A pending statement lock; the paper's Appendix B checked it only numerically; no analytic proof of the zeta-monotonicity of Eq. (13) found in the literature search, which was not systematic); (ii) Eq. (1) holds for every engine of Eqs. (3)-(4) (Lean machine check of a known result). NOT proved: that eta~+ is attained, or that every engine with asymmetry zeta has eta/eta_C <= etaPlus(zeta) (derivation + numerics only). The identification etaPlus = Eq. (13) is outside Lean. No device or power-plant claim.

Float / high-precision scans, not proofs: root-form monotonicity grid 124,800 consecutive-zeta pairs at 60 digits (producer), 0 non-increasing; auditor 336,200 pairs (41 c x 41 P~ x 201 zeta, mpmath 40 digits), 0 non-increasing, smallest increment 1.25e-12; E3x implicit-differentiation grid of 801,900 points: d etaPlus/d zeta > 0, minimum 1.2e-5, maximum 0.34; 17,355 random exact-rational engines (producer) and 53,021 random engines (auditor) with 0 violations of Eq. (1) and 0 violations of eta/eta_C <= etaPlus(zeta) (max LHS of Eq. (1) 0.99999091, so the bound is nearly attained); the root form is a valid upper bound, NOT attained in general, on a brute-force float optimum of the engine at exactly given power (producer 8 points, root - brute in [4.8e-7, 2.2e-3]; auditor 8 other points, [1.3e-5, 6.6e-3]; all >= 0). The 53,021 engines are the only evidence that engine_bound's hypotheses are satisfiable.

(13) equals the root form; the + branch choice is numerical only; P~=0 and the endpoints Mh=0 / Mc=0 not formalised; a Lean example that engine_bound's hypotheses can be met; Esposito et al. 2010 not re-read; a systematic literature search; ordering of the preregistration against the work (hash matches).
